lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: compound events

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

items.prompt: A probability of 1 means an event is...

steps: Identify the favorable outcomes and the total possible outcomes.
Write the probability as a reduced fraction, or use it to predict or evaluate a count.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: A spinner was spun 50 times and landed on blue 9 times. Based on this experiment, what is the experimental probability of landing on blue?
A bag has 9 red, 10 blue, and 16 green marbles. If one marble is drawn at random, what is the theoretical probability of drawing red, P(red)?
A fair coin is flipped and a spinner with 5 equal sections numbered 1 to 5 is spun. What is the probability of getting tails on the coin and landing on 4 on the spinner?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A meal is made by choosing one main dish from 4 options and one side dish from 7 options. How many different meals are possible?

A probability model predicts a fair 5-section spinner lands on a chosen section about 41 times in 205 spins. A simulation of 205 spins landed on that section 46 times. How does the simulated count compare to the model's prediction?
An event has a probability of 1/10. How would you describe how likely the event is to happen?
choices: equally likely to happen or not happen

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.prompt: A spinner was spun 40 times and landed on blue 3 times. Based on this experiment, what is the experimental probability of landing on blue?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A bag has 7 red, 8 blue, and 13 green marbles. If one marble is drawn at random, what is the theoretical probability of drawing red, P(red)?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
